answer.rationale: Primary objective forbids raising delivery risk. Line is at 94% with no buffer and the contract does not auto-renew in 14 days, so a primary-vendor change, a second source that does not replace the expiring contract, or a deferral can stop the line; those disruption costs dominate unit-price TCO. Incumbent already refused a reopen, so negotiate_terms is unlikely this cycle. memory_c1 is the only action that historically preserved integration and scheduled deliveries. memory_c2 (low-cost switch worked last year) is the main contrary claim and is the one record worth verifying; even if confirmed, it does not speak to a no-buffer 94% line. memory_c5 month-to-month applied to non-critical spend, not this primary. Renew keeps risk flat; cost mandate is missed but TCO including stockout is not minimized by switching under these constraints.
